item: Quarantine dry run: a bounded, deterministic, read-only sample of titles and URLs per signal
summary: The dry run reported counts per signal and no rows, so the #1440 stub thresholds (fitted to four specimens and one example) could not be judged from it. The job now keeps up to 20 article ids per signal (SAMPLE_PER_SIGNAL, a display sample; 15 possible signals x 20 seven-digit ids measured at 3,063 bytes added to an 868-byte state file) as the candidates with the smallest sha256(signal:id), which depends only on signal and id so the same corpus gives the same rows in any chunk order and across pause, resume and restart; state holds ids only. GET /api/quarantine/samples joins them to id, title, URL and already-marked at read time (no body, snippet or keywords), reads a deleted row as present:false, clamps limit and says it is a spot-check, not an error rate. Read-only: write=true, import screening, include_stubs defaults and the release run are unchanged. 13 new tests, each red without its change.
